newsitem.title: UK: Ghana sold 2/3 of its main cocoa crop--official.
newsitem.headline: Ghana sold 2/3 of its main cocoa crop--official.

text.p: Ghana has sold just under 200,000 tonnes of its 1996/97 main crop cocoa still forecast at 300,000 tonnes, a senior official said on Monday.
John Newman, managing director of Ghana's cocoa board, said the country forecasts total crop at 330,000 tonnes including a light crop of around 30,000-35,000 tonnes.
Speaking to reporters before the International Cocoa Organisation (ICCO) talks in London, Newman said Ghana had about 50,000 tonnes more of the main crop to sell to the international market.
"We have to take account of our local processing that's going to be around 50,000 to 60,000 tonnes," he said.
Newman said the weather had been exceptionally dry in January and February but there had been rainfall a few weeks ago.
"It was quite dry even in the forest," he said.
Newman, criticising crop estimates based on the country's purchasing figures, said arrivals cannot be the key consideration.
"You have to look at whether the crop is coming from other than key areas and the price paid to the farmers," he said.
He said the arrival factor is not indicative of total production, adding that buyers were bringing the cocoa onto the market quickly to cash in profits.
But he said that the crop would tail off "in a couple of weeks".
So far, Ghanaian arrivals have totalled 281,558 tonnes to the end of the 17th week of the 1996/97 season. This compares with 318,371 tonnes in the corresponding year-ago period.
